top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu is the only writer in the slate, and on the common criteria I rank the proposal above no award. His voice is distinctive and carried by the sentence. His formal ambition holds across very large structures, as publicly described for the Blinding (Orbitor) trilogy and Solenoid. A single imaginative project joining memory, the body and dream recurs across a long career that begins in poetry. The citation is scoped to one writer and one language. It rests on the prose and names poetry as its root, without claiming the poetry has been assessed as a separate body of work. Real reservations remain. Romanian rhythm, syntax and sound patterning cannot be checked through translation. It is unsettled whether the late novels deepen the early project or partly repeat it. Translation coverage of the poetry and early prose is thin. I have not independently verified any text. These are limits on how fully the case can be tested, not a failure of a stated criterion, so they do not justify P000. The unanimity of the round-2 files is not evidence of merit, and I have not relied on it.
